title: Quant baseline recommender: workload fingerprinting + shadow calibration
creator: Aisha Park
description:
Goal: produce per-model recommended quantization defaults (FP8/INT8 profiles + conservative fallbacks) that can be published in the model catalog and enforced by rollout policies. This ticket scopes the recommender algorithm, calibration harness, validation metrics, and the automated canary flow for deployment.

Scope:
- Fingerprint workloads by token-distribution, sequence-length distro, and instruction/assistant mix so recommendations are workload-aware rather than global.
- Run shadow calibration for candidate profiles (FP8-fast, FP8-standard, INT8-conservative) on a sampled corpus and synthetic inversion tests to catch edge-case degradation.
- Define acceptance thresholds (relative metric deltas and sign tests) and an automated fallback to FP16 when thresholds fail.
- Produce a small per-model YAML of recommended default profile + confidence band + suggested rollout policy for Console ingestion.

Why different from existing efforts: we emphasize operational fingerprints and inversion-style stress tests (targeting logit collapse and instruction-following regressions) rather than purely dataset-average calibration. This is intended to reduce surprise regressions on tail workloads seen in prior calibrations.

Deliverables:
1) Recommender prototype notebook and CLI that outputs recommended profile + confidence string.
2) Calibration harness with synthetic inversion suite and shadow-run orchestration.
3) Validation report format (CSV + metadata) and example per-model YAML.
4) CI gating rule draft for quant-profile changes.

Trade-offs and decisions:
- Cost vs coverage: Shadow runs add GPU hours; we'll limit to two calibration shards per model for initial rollout and prioritize high-usage models.
- Threshold sensitivity: we pick conservative thresholds for first rollouts (see acceptance_criteria) to avoid customer-visible regressions.
- FP8 vs INT8: FP8 gives better throughput on supported kernels; INT8 fallback prioritized for models with brittle logits or instruction-following sensitivity.

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/123456789/Quant+Recommender, prototype notebook: drive.google.com/drive/fake-notebook-link, draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-recommender/pull/42
acceptance_criteria: Recommender produces a profile for a target model and returns a confidence classification (high/medium/low)
Calibration harness runs shadow job on sample corpus and synthetic inversion tests and emits the validation report

Automatic fallback decision: if relative delta of instruction-following score > 2.0% or token-level perplexity increases by >0.5, the recommended profile is marked as 'requires human review' and default falls back to FP16
Model YAML artifact created and ingestible by the Console model-catalog API
CI gating rule blocks PRs that change the recommended profile for high-confidence models without a recorded shadow validation report
comments: 2025-11-13 Miguel: Initial scoping review — agreed on fingerprint dimensions (token skew, seq-len P50/P90, prompt vs assistant ratio). Will prototype fingerprint extractor this week.

2025-11-30 Kate Li (Research): Calibration run found subtle increase in hallucination rate on a 300-sample instruction set for FP8-standard on rwd-llama-variant; recommended INT8-conservative pending further sampling.
2025-12-02 PM review (Evan): Request to include 'observed throughput improvement' metric in the validation report to help cost tradeoff conversations.
2025-12-03 Miguel: Updated harness to include throughput delta and added a flag for 'cost-sensitivity' in the output YAML.
decision_log: 2025-11-15: Chose three candidate profile families: FP8-fast (aggressive latency), FP8-standard (balanced), INT8-conservative (safety-first).
2025-11-20: Acceptance threshold set: instruction-following delta <= 2% (relative), token-level perplexity change <= 0.5 absolute. Exceeding either triggers human review.
2025-11-27: Canary rollout policy drafted: 0% -> 5% shadow traffic -> 1% live canary -> 10% live canary (monitor 48h) -> ramp. Automatic rollback on any major-safety regression.
